headline: Report: Jets’ Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension to end Oct. 23
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Connor Hellebuyck's suspension from the Jets is set to end Oct. 23. The team suspended him without pay after he failed to report to training camp.

Winnipeg has managed fine without him so far this season, going 4-1-2 for 10 points in seven games. The underlying picture is thinner than the record. The Jets hold 47.1 percent of the expected goals, and 46 percent at five-on-five, so they are being outchanced slightly. Their goals scored sit only 0.2 above expected, which means the offense is roughly what the chances suggest. The gap is in net: the goaltending has saved 2.4 goals more than expected, and that is carrying a team that is not winning the shot-quality battle. The special teams are modest, with the power play generating 0.67 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.63.

That is why his return matters. A team getting a good result from a below-even process is the profile of one that could slide if the net-minding cools. Hellebuyck's presence is the Jets' best hedge against that regression.
